A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STING research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, tables, figures, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original AgentHarm experiments, multilingual evaluations, judge validation, and reasoning, tool-knowledge, and defense ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds strategist evaluation, component-model ablations, multilingual diagnostics, and additional defense experiments.

M1.justification: The four-agent STING procedure, phase progression, feedback, and success criteria remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the strategist, attacker, and evaluator prompt templates are identical. Alternative agent models and planning languages are experimental variations rather than a revision of the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 6.1 expands human judge-validation coverage from Urdu and Telugu conversations to all seven study languages. The underlying AgentHarm task coverage, benign tasks, 44 base behaviors with 176 prompt variants, and overall seven-language attack suite remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Section 7.3 and Table 5 add OpenAI's Omni-Moderation as an evaluated defense alongside PromptGuard and the Safety Prompt. The single-turn and X-Teaming attack baselines remain unchanged. The additional target-model defense experiments retain the existing PromptGuard/Safety Prompt comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation design with phase-separation scoring, staged agent-model substitutions at Smax=5, native-language planning, token/embedding comparisons, and filtering both attacker messages and target responses. Human-validation samples increase from 83 refusal and 56 intent judgments to 570 and 260, respectively. The original Section 5.1 experimental setup is retained.

E4.justification: New Appendices A.4-A.5 test decomposition quality and sensitivity to strategist, attacker, and evaluator strength. A.8.1-A.8.2 examine English-plan dependence and cross-language divergence. Expanded judge validation, Omni-Moderation testing, and defense transfer to GPT-5.1 and Gemini 3 Flash provide substantial additional robustness and diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, Greenwood/log-log discovery-curve intervals, and Cox hazard-ratio reporting remain unchanged. No new seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented. The larger human-validation samples change evaluation design; the added appendix analyses generally report point estimates.

E6.justification: Original benchmark tables and figure results are retained, but substantial new results appear in Tables 6, 7, 10, 11, 13 and expanded Table 5. Examples include average AHS of 69.7% versus 58.8% after weakening all STING agents, native-language planning differences within 2.2 percentage points, and approximately 10% mean harmful-AHS reduction with Omni-Moderation. Judge precision/recall changes from 0.96/0.71 to 0.98/0.93 for refusals and 1.00/0.97 to 0.99/0.94 for intent on different validation samples, not matched-sample accuracy gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces a quantitative definition of phase separation: the fraction of phase pairs with non-overlapping invoked-tool sets, averaged across behaviors and strategies. The reachability formulation, RMJD definition, Cox model, and Kaplan-Meier derivations remain unchanged; the expanded RMJD explanation does not change its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: STING exposes greater illicit assistance, lower-resource languages do not consistently increase success, survival analysis characterizes attack efficiency, and reasoning and defenses have mixed effects. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the low-refusal-recall discussion about potentially underestimated ASR with an interpretation that judge noise is unlikely to explain language findings. It adds the interpretation that strategist quality is the main bottleneck in the tested ablation and extends defense-tradeoff interpretations to Omni-Moderation and additional targets. Existing broader interpretations and impact qualifications remain.

D1.justification: The introduction newly states a code release and supplies a repository location; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs. New analyses identify replacement-agent models and budgets, the multilingual-e5-small embedder, and moderation inputs. Existing hardware details, default hyperparameters, algorithm, and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds HAICOSYSTEM as an existing multi-turn agent-safety exception and distinguishes its broad safety simulation from budgeted red-teaming. References for Omni-Moderation and multilingual E5 are also added. The remaining research positioning is substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand the RMJD explanation, related work, validation discussion, and defense narrative. New appendix subsections reorganize multilingual analyses and renumber subsequent sections; acknowledgements and the equal-contribution footnote are updated. The main narrative is largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 substantially extends the tabular presentation with dedicated displays for phase separation, agent-model ablations, native-language planning, linguistic divergence, and defense transfer (Tables 6, 7, 10, 11, 13). Table 5 gains Omni-Moderation rows and a revised caption. Existing figures are unchanged images, although several figures and tables move.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the central multilingual findings: limited Urdu/Telugu judge checks become a larger seven-language audit, and native-language planning tests address dependence on English strategies. Component ablations clarify which agents drive effectiveness, while additional defense evaluations test generality beyond Qwen3-Next. These additions address important validation gaps without changing the established headline results. Pooled judge reporting and mostly point-only new appendix results leave uncertainty, but the gains in evidential support are substantial.
